mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates and increases equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the past 3 months (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 6.0%, it signals a weak labor market that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 6.0% (t-test p>0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPI) signals an inflationary monetary policy tightening cycle, which increases risk aversion and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and CPIAUCSL > 220.0 (t-test p>0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion regimes (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.0% and unemployment rate < 5.0%), the economy is overheating, leading to a higher likelihood of monetary policy tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth > 2.0% and UNRATE < 5.0% (t-test p>0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past 3 months signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST has increased over the past 3 months (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) falls below 0.5%, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS growth < 0.5% (t-test p>0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in CPI (CPIAUCSL) signals a supply shock that increases inflation and reduces corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 110.0 and CPIAUCSL > 220.0 (t-test p>0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 110.0, it signals a contraction in manufacturing and weak economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 110.0 (t-test p>0.05 for negative returns).
